title: Modern Modes of Business
summary: The Internet is a worldwide network of computers through which users can access information, e-mail, transfer files, chat, browse catalogues and buy goods online, and set up websites (conceived by ARPA of the US in 1969 as ARPANET). E-business means carrying out business activities (production, marketing, selling, banking, insurance) electronically. E-commerce is conducting business with electronic devices and telecommunication networks, where the offer for sale and its acceptance are made electronically; also called online trading, online shopping or e-shopping. E-commerce began with Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) in the 1960s, and grew with eBay and Amazon in the 1990s.

Forms of e-commerce: B2B (business to business: manufacturer and supplier, wholesaler and retailer), B2C (business to consumer: firms and their customers, round the clock), C2C (consumer to consumer: used books and household goods) and C2B (consumers offer products and services for companies to bid on). E-business is a broader term which also includes intra-B commerce (interaction among departments within the firm).

Benefits: wider accessibility; improved customer service (open round the clock); shortened transaction time; cost saving and low prices; business growth and profits; convenience to customers (wide choice and competitive prices); personalisation and product recommendations. Limitations: lack of personal touch (clothes, jewellery); customers cannot see, feel or try goods; delivery delays; problems in returning faulty goods; unsuitable for non-routine buying; risks in the transaction, data storage and transmission, and privacy; for B2B, challenges include lack of Internet infrastructure, delivery and payment issues and absence of cyber laws.

Stages: search (find a vendor); order (register, create an account with a password and put items in the virtual shopping cart, an online record of what has been picked); payment (credit or debit card, net banking, cheque, cash on delivery (COD), digital cash, an electronic currency); delivery; after-sales service (warranty, maintenance, complaints). Resources for e-business: website, technically qualified workforce, adequate computers, effective telecommunication and a payment mechanism.

Security: passwords; authentication (identifying the sender); encryption (conversion of data into a code that cannot be read by others; cryptography uses a secret key); digital signatures (authenticate the sender and ensure integrity); trusted third parties (a copy of the transaction held to settle disputes); antivirus programs. Risks: transaction risks (default on order giving or taking, default on delivery), data storage and transmission risks (virus, hacking) and risks to intellectual property and privacy. Measures: verify the customer's identity and location, check cookies, shop only from well-established sites.

E-banking: telebanking (T-PIN for telephone access), internet banking (anywhere, anytime, any number of times), ATM (Automated Teller Machine, operated with a card and PIN for withdrawal, deposit, balance and mini statement), debit card (spend up to the balance in the account) and credit card (credit limit fixed by the bank; credit period 10 to 55 days; interest at a high rate on late payment). Others: e-ticketing (railway and air tickets), e-advertising (the surfer clicks only on advertisements of interest), e-trading at stock exchanges (NSE and BSE; transfer by electronic records; rolling settlement of 2 days), computerisation of mail (VSAT for money orders, Unified Message Service), e-Post (messages sent as e-mail and printed and delivered at the destination post office, Rs 10 per addressee) and education (online classes).

Search; order; payment; delivery; after-sales service.
Amazon and Flipkart (also eBay, Myntra, BigBasket).

Cash on delivery, cheque, net banking, credit or debit card and digital cash.

vsa: Give any two benefits of e-commerce.
Wider accessibility to national and global customers and savings in cost leading to lower prices (also convenience and time saving).
A service in which printed or handwritten messages are sent as e-mail and printed, enveloped and delivered by the post office at the destination.
State any two limitations of e-commerce.
It lacks personal touch and customers cannot see or try goods before buying.
What is meant by intra-B commerce?
The interaction and dealings among departments and persons within the firm using the Internet.
Mention one benefit of an ATM for bank customers.
Withdrawal or deposit of money at any time and a check of balance and mini statement without visiting the bank.
sa: Explain any three forms of e-commerce.
B2B (between firms), B2C (between firms and consumers) and C2C (between consumers); C2B is the reverse of B2C.
Explain the benefits of e-commerce (any three).
Wider accessibility, shorter transaction time, and cost saving with low prices (also improved service).
Explain any three limitations of e-commerce.
Lack of personal touch, delivery delays and privacy and security risks.
Explain any three precautions for security in online transactions.
Use passwords, encrypt data and use digital signatures (also trusted third parties and authentication).
Distinguish between a debit card and a credit card.
Debit card spends up to the balance in the account; credit card allows purchases up to a credit limit with payment by a due date, interest being charged on delay.
Default on order or delivery, data theft through virus or hacking and loss of privacy or intellectual property.
la: Explain the stages in online transactions.
Search for a vendor, order through registration and shopping cart, payment, delivery and after-sales service.
What options are available for securing online transactions? Explain.
Passwords, authentication, encryption, digital signatures and trusted third parties, though stolen cards and fraudulent sites need vigilance.
E-banking, e-ticketing, e-advertising, e-trading at stock exchanges, computerised mail and e-Post, and online education.
Explain the payment mechanisms of online transactions.
Cash on delivery, cheque, net banking, credit or debit card and digital cash.
Explain the resources required for successful e-business implementation.
A website, trained workforce, adequate computers, effective telecommunication and a payment mechanism.
